answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol anchors identity nodes across a cryptographic reef of stake. Each new agent requires burning verifiable stake, scaling costs superlinearly via f(n)=k*n^2. Like planting a hardy juniper atop a barren knoll, an attacker attempting to register multiple identities faces quadratic economic friction, rendering large-scale spoofing mathematically unviable as aggregate coordination costs escalate exponentially.
